question: What is the atomicity of Chlorine?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Diatomic.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Chlorine** exists as a** diatomic molecule,** which means it consists of** two atoms of chlorine** joined by a **covalent bond.**
 
• The symbol for chlorine is Cl, and its atomic number is** 17, **which means it has **17 protons and 17 electrons **in its nucleus and shells, respectively.
 
• Chlorine is a** halogen**, and it is a **highly reactive nonmetal **that can form compounds with many other elements.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tetra-atomic** is a rare type of molecule that consists of **four atoms** of the same or different elements.
 
• Examples include s**ulfur tetrafluoride (SF4)** and **phosphorus tetraiodide (PI4).**
 
• **Poly-atomic molecules** are common in chemistry and include many organic compounds such as **glucose (C6H12O6) and DNA (deoxyribonucleic acid).**
 
• **Monoatomic**** **elements are rare and include **noble gases** such as **helium (He) and neon (Ne),** which exist as single atoms and **do not form** molecules with other atoms.
